column11: the course as a whole didn't feel very cohesive. there were essentially 4 different parts to it: discussions, lectures & exams, R coding labs, and the final project. we did not do any coding in lecture so for the lab homeworks it kind of felt like we were just being thrown to the wolves. the discussions were usually about random papers that we were required to read that also didn't really have anything to do with the lecture. the lab homeworks were very difficult, they got me so frustrated, and this is coming from someone who has a background in the R programming software we used. i can't imagine how my classmates felt who didn't have any background in the program. i think if this course is going to stay as it is, they should require an R programming class as a prereq (although that didn't even really help me), or the instructor needs to have one of the first classes be explaining how the software works. cause they did not even teach us how to use the software so that was a big issue. the many times i did go to office hours, most of the class was there. i think this says a lot, and maybe the labs should have been done together in class.

column48:
for the most part, i understood what was expected of me. the instructor did a good job some classes writing the plan for the class period up on the board, so we knew how our time was going to be used that day.  however, when we got to the final projects portion of the course, i was more confused and didn't really understand what i was doing or what i actually needed to submit
i appreciated that we got a break in the class period, as sometimes there was a lot of information to swallow so a break was needed.
i was looking forward to taking this course because i had already taken Intro to R Programming and i really liked it because i enjoyed using the software. this course killed that enjoyment because the coding was so hard. it's very clear this course is a work in progress but i think it has a lot of potential to be so much better
i also didn't appreciate how the professor essentially extended the class period. they claimed that there was a scheduling error and that the registrar's office "messed up" since it's a 4 credit course and there was no additional lab section (like how it typically is for the science classes; a 3 credit lecture, 1 credit lab section). even though the course description said the 1 credit lab would take place online, the professor made us stay an extra 45 minutes on some class days as our own lab section, which seemed unfair cause i registered for a class that fit in my schedule and then the professor decided that they needed it to be longer.
